alternative by shifting recommendation to an active, user-side par-
adigm, where generative agents autonomously perceive external
platforms, reason over user preferences, and execute decisions.

HTML, ReMem observes item pages through screenshots and ex-

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Held-out leave-one-out test sets are scored with objective HR@K and NDCG@K metrics, and the judging task uses an LLM-as-judge accuracy check against ground-truth items.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcome is established by HR@K, NDCG@K, and LLM-as-judge accuracy on held-out test splits.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Multi-Memory GRPO training is driven by format rewards plus task-specific correctness rewards computed from ground-truth items using HR@K, NDCG@K, and accuracy.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported gains (such as an overall 5.16% average improvement over top baselines and superior retention over long context lengths) are supported by empirical results across tasks, while trade-offs like increased inference latency are clearly documented.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Experiments evaluate ReMem across three Amazon-derived benchmark datasets (Games, Books, MovieTV) on Searching, Ranking, and Judging tasks, comparing against sequential recommenders, LLM recommenders, agentic systems, and long-context models with ablations and varying-length context analysis.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective ranking and retrieval metrics (HR@K, NDCG@K) on held-out leave-one-out interaction test sets evaluate model performance separately from RL training rollouts.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The final evaluation on held-out test splits is measured via standard objective recommendation metrics (HR@K, NDCG@K) and an LLM-as-judge accuracy check on the judging task.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Policy training uses Multi-Memory GRPO driven by format rewards and objective task correctness against ground-truth items (Hit Rate, NDCG, Accuracy/LLM-as-judge string match).

primary.limitations: The authors identify high inference latency stemming from sequential chunk updates as a practical limitation and outline future directions toward richer multi-action environments and varied chunking schedules.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the OCR-driven item card conversion, the chunked memory update equations bounded in token space, and the Multi-Memory GRPO objective with group advantage propagation and KL regularization.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a coherent framework addressing both perception noise and long-context degradation in recommender agents, supported by explicit mathematical formulation, ablations, baseline comparisons, and honest analysis of latency constraints.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces ReMem, a recommendation agent framework that couples OCR-based visual item parsing with a chunk-wise time-evolving natural language memory and a multi-memory GRPO variant that propagates final recommendation advantage to intermediate memory updates.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a coherent framework addressing both perception noise and long-context degradation in recommender agents, supported by explicit mathematical formulation, ablations, baseline comparisons, and honest analysis of latency constraints.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors identify high inference latency stemming from sequential chunk updates as a practical limitation and outline future directions toward richer multi-action environments and varied chunking schedules.
